clue.text: Bargain on standard vegetable

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece written on another follows it

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
a snip is a bargain, something cheap

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a cut-price vegetable of the usual quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the bargain after the standard.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root eaten cooked is a familiar vegetable.

clue.text: One escaped from Slough, another went to Kent

definitions.meaning: Christian in Bunyan's allegory escaped the Slough of Despond on his journey
Chaucer's travellers rode to Canterbury in Kent to visit a shrine

explanation.surface: Two people leaving places in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the Berkshire town, but it is Bunyan's Slough of Despond in The Pilgrim's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Bunyan's hero and Chaucer's Canterbury travellers are religious wayfarers journeying to holy ends.

clue.text: Substance on butt of cigar retained by stern doctor

indicators.note: retained by means held inside, so the stern goes round the other letters

parts.note: the rear is the stern, the back part

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: the gist is the substance or main point

indicators.note: the butt of a cigar is its end, so take its last letter

explanation.surface: A stern doctor confiscates a substance found on a cigar stub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like an adjective describing the doctor; it is the back of a ship. A REGISTRAR is a British hospital doctor grade, which is fair for 'doctor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is a hospital doctor in a senior training grade below consultant.

clue.text: Comparatively attractive name Eric changed

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of Eric are reordered

explanation.surface: A man called Eric has had a makeover and looks better.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, meaning more pleasant or appealing.

clue.text: Diatribe from Greek character with sauce and endless pluck

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lip is cheek or sauce, insolent talk

indicators.note: endless says the word for pluck loses its final letter

parts.note: to pick is to pluck, as a string or fruit

explanation.surface: A rant from a cheeky, bold Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' and 'pluck' read as cheek and courage; they give LIP and PICK, docked to PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A philippic is a bitter verbal attack, named after Demosthenes' speeches against Philip of Macedon.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: about says the row goes round the straying word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over a dog that has wandered off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats, and 'about' signals that it wraps the straying word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breed bred for hunting burrowing animals is a type of dog.

clue.text: Same number from North and South meeting in the middle, in principle

indicators.note: the two readings meet and share their middle letter, so one copy of it goes

parts.note: ten is a number

indicators.note: read from the South, a down entry goes upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the same number, ten again

explanation.surface: A rule that holds whether you read it top to bottom or bottom to top.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN read down and TEN read up from the South overlap on their shared N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true.

clue.text: Place for bets people put on dog, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
to dog someone is to track or follow them

explanation.surface: Punters bet on a dog at the greyhound stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on dog' reads as betting on a greyhound; 'dog' is the verb TRACK, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example of that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse is where punters gamble on horses or dogs, a venue for wagering.

clue.text: Like many a column, wry, with no end of humour

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so that letter is removed from the wry word

parts.note: wry humour is ironic

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of humour

explanation.surface: A dry newspaper column that has run out of jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' looks journalistic but is architectural; R, the last letter of 'humour', leaves IRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionic order, with scroll-shaped capitals, is one of the classical styles of pillar.

clue.text: Let engaging English queen come back on stage

indicators.note: engaging means holding, so the rent word takes in the English letter

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it out
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A queen in a play is allowed to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to make a fresh entrance, as an actor returning to the boards.

clue.text: Reason soldier's used to stop colonel retreating

indicators.note: a piece used to stop a gap is put inside it, here inside the turned abbreviation
retreating says the colonel's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A soldier is sent to block a colonel's withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns COL into LOC, and 'used to stop' plugs GI into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning, the faculty of argument, is a synonym of reason.

clue.text: Greenness at one time surrounding church beside pub

indicators.note: beside joins the two parts side by side

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for 'at one time' goes round the church

parts.note: once means at one time, formerly
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A village scene of long ago: a green round the church, with the pub next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenness' is naivety, not grass; 'surrounding' wraps the 'at one time' word round the church to give OCENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenness is inexperience, the naive lack of worldliness of the young.

clue.text: Militiaman stirs, ever prepared

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A part-time soldier rouses himself, always ready for duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' looks like part of the picture of readiness but rearranges STIRS EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-time soldier held in reserve for call-up is like a militiaman.

clue.text: Old history master wanting us to be silent

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letters of us are removed

parts.note: Tacitus was a great Roman historian
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly history teacher tells the class to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old history master' sounds like a schoolteacher but means the Roman historian TACITUS; 'wanting' drops US.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without being said aloud in words.

clue.text: Painting of maiden by river

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A picture of a young woman standing by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a painting done directly on a wall.

clue.text: Rings to offer support, in the main

definitions.text: Rings to offer support, in the main

parts.words: Rings to offer support, in the main
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and these rings keep people afloat in it

explanation.surface: Telephone calls offering help, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly' but means at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring-shaped buoys thrown to people in the water hold them up.

clue.text: Warship's run alongside one vessel in lord's possession

indicators.note: in says the run, one and vessel go inside the lord
in the lord's possession means held within the lord's letters

parts.note: a peer is a lord

indicators.note: alongside sets the run next to the next pieces

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one
a vat is a large vessel for liquids

explanation.surface: A nobleman owns a warship, along with a single tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' and 'one' look like verbs and numbers in a sea story; 'in lord's possession' is the container signal, wrapping the lord's letters round the rest after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A privately owned armed ship licensed to attack enemy shipping was a kind of warship.

clue.text: Marker that shows opening of cave in country hill

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the country

parts.note: India is a country

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of cave

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A sign points to a cave entrance in a hilly land.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer or gauge that displays a reading is a marker that reveals something.

clue.text: Conductor chosen went on bus, say

parts.note: elect means chosen
rode means travelled on, a bus being one example

explanation.surface: A selected conductor took the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' suggests a bus conductor but means an electrical one.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a conductor through which current enters or leaves.

clue.text: Shameless farce, with a terribly wearing plot

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the bed goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: a bed is a plot of garden ground

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of farce and a are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A theatre critic finds a farce brazen, with a dreadfully tiring storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is not a storyline but a patch of garden; 'terribly' rearranges the farce and a into AREFAC, and 'wearing' sets that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Barefaced means openly brazen, done without any shame or disguise.

clue.text: Coarse fabric with damage raised under a dollar

indicators.note: under puts the turned word below the dollar in a down clue

parts.note: a buck is slang for a dollar

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: Coarse cloth with flaws is marked up to a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns MAR to RAM, which goes below BUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff cotton or linen cloth used in bookbinding.

clue.text: Observes guards

definitions.meaning: ... a rule or festival means observes it
castle strongholds or towers are ..., also called guards in a sense of protection

explanation.surface: Someone watches and protects.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a custom is to observe it; a castle's keeps are its strongholds that guard it.

clue.text: Painter, by the sound of it, superior to Constable

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a police sergeant ranks above a constable

explanation.surface: An artist said to outrank Constable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the painter John Constable, matching 'Painter', but it is the police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated American portrait artist.

clue.text: Article in copy is early one from WI1

indicators.note: in says the article goes inside the copy word

parts.note: to crib is to copy
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing copied turns out to be by an early West Indian.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the West Indies, so the definition means an early inhabitant of those islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs were among the native peoples of the Caribbean when Europeans arrived.

clue.text: Quick to knock half-formed notion

parts.note: to rap is to knock

indicators.note: half-formed means only half of the word for notion is used

parts.note: an idea is a notion

explanation.surface: Quick to criticise a half-baked idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' reads as criticise but gives RAP; ID is the first half of IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or swift.

clue.text: Non-stop flight?

parts.note: not a plane journey but a flight of stairs that keeps moving without stopping

explanation.surface: An air journey with no stopovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase is a flight of steps in constant motion.

clue.text: Adversary in Troy Menelaus upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Menelaus, upset at Troy, faces his foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden letters, and 'upset' reads them upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An enemy is a foe or opponent.

clue.text: Destroyer abandoning last position

indicators.note: abandoning last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a locust destroys crops

explanation.surface: A warship leaves its final position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' looks like a warship but is the crop-eating LOCUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a place or site, a position.

clue.text: Odious traveller advanced, bagging first pair, of elephants

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the traveller-and-advanced pair holds the letters

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller
advanced money is lent

indicators.note: first pair takes the opening two letters of the word elephants

explanation.surface: A salesman who lent money is found carrying off a couple of elephants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odious' alone is the definition; 'bagging' sets the opening pair of 'elephants' between the traveller and the advanced money.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent is disgusting, causing aversion, much like odious.

clue.text: Spice chapter with passion

parts.note: love is passion

explanation.surface: A cookbook chapter devoted to spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloves are dried flower buds used as a pungent spice.

clue.text: Way pen conveys diffidence

parts.note: mode is a way or manner
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: Someone's style of writing shows a shy reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' is not a writing tool but a pig STY.
explanation.definitionFit: Modesty is shy reserve about oneself, a lack of self-assertion like diffidence.

clue.text: Particular honour

definitions.meaning: a ... is a particular point, as in 'in every ...'
to honour someone is to hold them in high regard

explanation.surface: A detail and an esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: In one respect means in one particular detail; respect is also esteem shown to someone.
